original_caption: \caption{The regular pentagon is a two-distance set: sides (charcoal) and diagonals (coral). In the plane no two-distance set has more than $5$ points (Kelly, 1947). Theorem~\ref{combinatorial:thm:twodist} gives $9$, Blokhuis' refinement $6$.}
interim_caption:
\caption{The regular pentagon has two distances: side lengths (charcoal)
and diagonal lengths (coral). The first span count below gives an upper
bound of $9$ points in the plane; the proved affine-function refinement
improves it to $6$. This drawing supplies a five-point example.}
current_caption:
\caption{The regular pentagon has two distances: side lengths (charcoal)
and diagonal lengths (coral). The first span count below gives $9$ points
in the plane and the affine-function refinement gives $6$.
Proposition~\ref{combinatorial:prop:planarmax} proves the sharp maximum $5$,
attained by this drawing.}
